payload.text: Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Ninety-six, señor? No. I move again, as a courtesy: seventy-eight P. The card belongs in my Salamanca album, and I am paying properly for it. Let us not spoil a pleasant afternoon.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres... pero no me enfado, nunca me enfado. Cinco primas, cariño, y de corazón. El Portero no me da para más hoy. Anda, ve a ver a El Chato con tus repetidos, y luego vuelve a contarme. ¿Seguro que has desayunado?

¡Amigo, se acabó el baile! La Puerta de Alcalá, la auténtica, 143 P. Y es la última palabra de los Pícaros: si dices que no, cerramos la maleta y no nos ves más. La policía... digo, el taxi ya está arrancando. ¡Decide ahora mismo, hombre!

¡Cuarenta y siete! Nando, don't laugh, it hurts him. Amigo, listen — the police... I mean, the taxi! The taxi is waiting, motor running, driver shouting. Sixty pesos, El Marqués, warm from the suitcase, and your face still brings luck. Decide now or we're smoke. ¿Sí?

Buenas tardes. You have arrived at a good moment — I am seeking El Marqués, a Salamanca piece of real distinction. I offer seventy for it. A fair figure, señor, and I do not haggle like a market trader.

¡Seis! Nando, sujétame que me caigo. Mire, jefe, ayer un señor se llevó tres por lo mismo y volvió llorando de alegría. Cuatro primas, la Plaza del Dos de Mayo, y nos damos la mano antes de que cierre el mercado. Cuatro. Ni una menos, ni una más. ¿Venga?
Done! 5 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!
Ninety-three remains a fantasy, señor. Eighty-one P — I climb once more, slowly, as a lady should. El Marqués enters the safe this very afternoon, beside his neighbours. Shall we finish elegantly?

Ay, cariño, qué cabezón eres... pero me caes bien. Cinco primas, hijo, es lo que tengo para El Portero. Llévate las cinco y un abrazo. Y no olvides: El Chato abre a las nueve y media, le gustan los que cambian con honradez. ¿Has comido ya, corazón?
Veinticuatro... señor, you descend like a feather, very slowly. Eighteen primas — that is my last elegance of the evening. Las Vistillas is no El Retiro, and no amount of patience will make it so.

Ay, cariño, nine now? You never give up, eh? I like that, but my purse she is small and the bread she is expensive. Look — El Tatuador, five P, and your album begins today. Take him home, ¿sí, hijo? And eat something, you are too thin.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Amigo, basta — Nando, close the case. Listen: they stopped printing El Marqués yesterday, finished, no more, ever. Fifty-eight pesos. That is my last word, truly the last — say sí now or we walk, and you watch us disappear into the crowd forever. ¿Sí?

Ay, cariño, no, no — guarda ese dinero. Five P is my price, and five P it stays. Buy yourself a bocadillo with the rest, you look hungry.

Take it, and go see El Chato later. He trades fair, like my Manolo did.
Señor, serie doce de treinta — sí, conozco la tirada mejor que usted. Noventa y cinco es fantasía. Setenta y uno, y lo digo con afecto por la pieza, no por el regateo. ¿Cerramos?

¡Cincuenta y dos! Paco, guarda eso... No, espera. Jefe, escucha: hace nada vino otro equipo y nos ofreció mucho más por este mismo Ángel. Les dije que no, porque tú llegaste primero. Cincuenta y nueve primas y es tuyo, envuelto. ¡Venga, que el tren silba!
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Twenty-three, señor? You inch along like a Sunday paseo. Nineteen primas — and I say it with a sigh. Las Vistillas will never be El Retiro, however gracefully you descend. Decide, por favor; the hour grows late.

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show him — La Puerta de Alcalá, mint, beautiful, yes? For you, 187 P. And listen, hermano, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Nando checked every stall. Gone, finito. Touch it, feel that gold edge!

¡Ay, amigo, qué pena! Nos has caído bien, de verdad, pero hoy no sale. Cerramos la maleta sin rencor, eh, ni una palabra mala. Otro día te contamos la historia de esta carta con un café. Suerte, hombre... ¡que el taxi ya arranca de verdad! ¡Hasta la próxima, campeón!
Eighty-four P, señor. That is my last word — I shall not move again. Accept, and El Marqués rests in the Salamanca album tonight. Refuse, and I wish you a very good afternoon elsewhere.

¡Ahí está, sobre la mesa! Alfonso XII, rara, sesenta y tres y es tuya, primo. Nosotros vendemos raras a sesenta y tres, épicas a ciento sesenta y dos, y te compramos comunes y poco comunes si traes de sobra en la mochila. ¿Cerramos o sigues mirando el estanque?
Oh, you're killing us. 164 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
Buenas tardes. I know the card. My terms: La Puerta de Alcalá, ciento trece. Take your time — I am in no hurry.

¡Ay, hijo, eight! You come down one peseta each time, like a little clock. But no, cariño, my purse she stays closed. El Tatuador, five P — that is my offer, and a good one. Take him, start your album, and go eat something caliente.

"¡Amigo! Paco, Nando, mucho gusto — come, come, close the case before the wind takes it. El Marqués, here, for 73 P. And listen — the team at the next stall already asked for him twice this morning... but we like your face better. Decide quick, eh?"

¡Ay, hija, qué terca eres! Pero no, no — five P, ni un céntimo más. Me da vergüenza cobrarte catorce por una cartita.

Toma, Té Moruno, cinco P. Guarda el resto para un bocadillo, que estás muy flaca. Y luego pásate por El Chato, cariño.

¡Cincuenta y tres! Nando, dame la mano que me tiemblan las piernas. Jefe, mira: cincuenta y cuatro primas. Una sola prima nos separa, ¡una! Por una prima no me vas a dejar aquí llorando en el andén. Cincuenta y cuatro y lo envuelvo ahora mismo. ¡Venga, dame la mano!
Veintidós, señor. Basta. Twenty primas — my last word of the evening, and I shall not say it twice. Refuse, and I close my album and wish you buenas noches. Decide now, por favor.

"¡Amigo! Paco, look who walks up — a person with taste!" "A connoisseur, Nando, I saw it at once. Come, come, the case is open only this morning."

Té Moruno, fresh from the south, mint still breathing. Four P, for you, today only. Shall we wrap it?
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one — Mural de la Esquina — for you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
Señor, noventa sigue siendo fantasía, y la fantasía no cabe en mi caja fuerte. Setenta y tres, y lo digo por el cariño que tengo a Salamanca, no por usted. ¿Cerramos de una vez?

¡Ay, siete! Cariño, you will arrive at one peseta by Christmas, and still I say the same. My purse, she sleeps. El Tatuador, five P — pretty card, your album starts today. Take him, hijo, and go eat something hot, por favor.

¡Un regular! Paco, hear that — he comes back, he brings friends, he brings his cousin from Sevilla! For such a man, 151 P. Nando's hands are shaking, we have a train, the suitcase is closing. Take it, amigo, squeeze my hand and the gold is yours!

"¡Ay, forty-five! Paco nearly fainted —" "— he did, I caught him, amigo." Listen, we like you, so: 63 P for El Marqués, and that is us being generous before the other stall comes back waving coins. Say sí, we shake hands, you walk away a hero. Quick, quick!

¡Amigo! Paco here, Nando behind me — ¡Puesto del Rastro! The sweetest little stall card in the case, and it's yours for 4 P. But listen, listen: they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finished, done, no more coming. What's in the suitcase is all that exists. ¿Sí o sí?

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Trade gently, pay nothing extra: Fair Broker (v24) is 0% with a fair broker. El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 140 P.
Ciento trece. That was my term, and it remains my term. The card is clean, sí, but the number does not move. Think it over, señor.

"Forty-six! Nando, hold me —" "— I've got you, hermano." Amigo, listen: they stopped printing this one yesterday, finished, no more Marqués in this world. So, 57 P, final handshake, before that other stall comes running back. ¡Rápido, amigo, the wind is picking up!

Ay, cariño, no insistas — doce no, cinco P. Esa es mi palabra y no cambia.

Y un consejito: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas, hija! Luego te pasas por El Chato, abre a las nueve y media. ¿Has comido ya?

¡Ay, seis! Cariño, you are patient like me, but my purse she still sleeps. El Tatuador, five P — that is my song. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your repeated ones. ¿Has comido ya?
Psst. Museo Lázaro Galdiano. For you only, 73 P.

¡Qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo! No, no, guarda ese dinero. Para ti son cinco P, como dije. Yo no cambio mi palabra, cariño. Con lo que te sobra, cómprate algo de comer, que vienes flaco. Y acuérdate: cambia tus repetidas, así llenas la página entera.
Amigo! La Sala Pentagrama, 187 P, a gift, a real gift!

"Nando, he offers twenty!" "Paco, we are honest men — nearly." Amigo, we said four P and four P it stays. Keep your coins for churros. Té Moruno, fresh mint, four P, in your hands before the clock turns. ¿Lo envolvemos?
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 66 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Señor, ochenta y cinco no entra en mis álbumes. Setenta y cinco, y es mi última palabra. Si la rechaza, me levanto, cierro la caja fuerte y buscamos otro Marqués. Decida usted, por favor.

"Forty-seven! Paco, the wind, it took his coins —" "— no, hermano, he's just careful." Amigo, we like careful men. So: 52 P. That's us cutting into our own dinner, verdad. Shake now, before the other stall comes back waving their fat purse. ¡Rápido, sí?"
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 167 P.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: SAL-01 Escaparate de Serrano: venta a 6 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 1 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / SAL-01 Escaparate de Serrano: ask 6 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 1 P apar
Buenas. You find me at my desk, as always. La Puerta de Alcalá — the true one — leaves this vault on one term: one hundred thirteen P. I do not haggle quickly.
Ciento trece, señor. You may walk the Gran Vía and return tomorrow; you will find the same number waiting on this desk.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 167 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

"¡Paco, otra vez! He throws eighteen at us like confetti!" "Nando, we are not thieves — only fast." Amigo, save your coins. The Té Moruno is four P, not one real more. Fresh mint, still breathing, straight from the south. Four P, and it's yours before the clock turns. ¿Lo envolvemos?

Paco: Forty? Amigo, my heart! Nando: Our hearts, plural! Look — Museo Lázaro Galdiano, 62 P, final, beautiful, yours. Paco: And hurry, the poli— I mean, our taxi is waiting, motor running, driver shouting. Nando: He shouts terribly. Decide now, or it drives away with your bargain inside. ¡Venga!

"¡Hecho! Forty-eight, amigo — Paco, wrap him, quick, before I cry." "He's already crying, hermano." Take El Marqués, he's yours, and tell nobody what you paid, sí? Our mother would weep. ¡Un placer! Now go, go, before that other stall sees your face. ¡Adiós, amigo!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, El Tatuador, is a beauty — five P and he is yours. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates!
Señor, ya le di mi última palabra. Setenta y cinco era mi afecto por Salamanca; ochenta y tres es su fantasía. Cierro la caja fuerte. Buenas tardes, y que tenga usted suerte en otra parte.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 155 P.

Paco: Forty-four? Nando, hold me, I feel faint! Nando: I'm fainting too, hermano, we faint together. Paco: Listen — Museo Lázaro Galdiano, 58 P. Beautiful card, beautiful price, beautiful you. Nando: The taxi driver is now singing angry songs about us. Paco: He has a terrible voice. ¡Venga, amigo, 58!

Buenas tardes. I am afraid I have nothing further for you today — my albums are closed. Another day, perhaps, when something from Salamanca or El Retiro passes through your hands. Que tenga usted muy buena tarde.
Buenas tardes. I am afraid my albums are closed for today, señor. Nothing more will change hands at this stall. Do come another day — perhaps with something from Salamanca. It has been a pleasure.
